name: application-spending-insights-bar
title: Spending Insights Bar
description: Per-category spending bars with a tick marker at each category's historical average, colored by over/under status.
useWhen: Showing how this period's spending compares to a historical average across several categories at once.
You want the comparison legible from the bar alone (fill length + average tick) without requiring a tooltip or table.
Status (over/under/on average) should be readable through both color and position, not color alone.
avoidWhen: You're tracking a single budget against its limit — use `budget-progress-bar` for that one-category, threshold-based case.
You have more than 5-6 categories — this stacks vertically and gets long; use a proper bar chart with scroll or pagination instead.
There's no meaningful historical average to compare against — a plain spend-by-category list is more honest than a fabricated marker.
responsiveBehavior: Single-column card at a fixed max width; each category row's bar fills the available width, so the layout only changes via card width, not breakpoint-specific reflow.
accessibility: Each bar carries role=img with an aria-label stating the category, spent amount, average, and the over/under relationship in words, not just visually via bar length.
Status is encoded by both fill color and the bar's length relative to its average tick, so colorblind users can still read over/under from position.
The average tick marker is aria-hidden since its meaning is already stated in the bar's aria-label; it is a visual supplement, not a separate a11y unit.

variants.title: Spending Insights Bar
variants.description: Four spending categories (Groceries, Dining out, Transportation, Entertainment) each compared against a 6-month average.
accessibility: Over-average categories use red, under-average use emerald, and on-average uses neutral gray — a fixed three-way status mapping, not an arbitrary categorical palette.

variants.title: Spending Insights Bar (Dark)
variants.description: Spending insights bar adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Status colors are lifted to their -400 step and the average tick to gray-400 to hold WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
